name: NC-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with a +17 partisan lean
Incumbent Deborah Ross has a large financial advantage ($1.3M on hand vs. no reported fundraising for the Republican)
Prediction markets price Ross at about 99% to win
No competitive outside spending against the incumbent
model.rationale: This Raleigh-area seat leans Democratic by 17 points, and incumbent Deborah Ross holds a decisive money edge with no outside opposition spending and a Republican challenger who has not reported fundraising. Markets price her near certain to win, so the fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit margin.
model.watch: The forecast could shift only if polling emerged showing an unexpectedly competitive race or if outside groups began spending heavily against Ross.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Carolina's 2nd District, covering much of Raleigh and surrounding Wake County, leans Democratic by about 17 points. Deborah Ross, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term and has raised roughly $1.7 million with $1.3 million still on hand. Her Republican opponent, Eugene Douglass, has reported no fundraising, and a Libertarian is also on the ballot.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, but prediction markets give Ross about a 99 percent chance of winning. With no outside spending targeting the seat and the district's strong partisan lean, this is a Safe Democratic race with a projected margin of roughly 24 points.
